standards.name: Artifactory for Artifacts
test: Open the CI workflow files for five production services in GitHub Actions and list every artifact source and publish endpoint
Open the Repositories admin page in Artifactory and confirm each remote repo proxies an approved registry as sole outbound path
Open Xray scan results in Artifactory for three recent production images and record immutable tag, SHA digest and scan outcome
Run a docker pull from Docker Hub on a production-segment build agent and record whether the request is blocked
Pass when no public registry URLs appear, all 3 images show tag, digest and scan with no unresolved Criticals, and the pull fails

standards.name: Assumptions and Constraints
test: Open the project charter pages for five active projects in Confluence and locate the assumptions and constraints register in each
Check each register in Confluence for dated entries covering material assumptions and binding constraints
Open the page history in Confluence and confirm a dated planning-phase review or sign-off of each register after initiation
Open the risk register in the PPM tool (Planview) and trace any invalidated assumption to a risk entry with ID, owner and response
Open the charter template and gate workflow in the PPM tool (Planview) and confirm the section is required, never approved blank
Pass when all 5 charters hold a complete reviewed register and every uncertain assumption maps to an owned risk entry

standards.name: Atomic Commits
test: Open the commit list on the main integration branch in GitHub Enterprise and sample ten recent commits
Open each sampled commit diff in GitHub Enterprise and confirm it contains exactly one logical change with no unrelated files
Run git bisect between two release tags in a local clone (VS Code terminal) to isolate a known past defect and count the steps
Open Settings > Branches and the pull request template in GitHub Enterprise and confirm multi-concern commits are prohibited
Pass when all ten commits are single-concern, the bisect converges in eight or fewer steps, and guidelines bar mixed commits

standards.name: Auto-Generated From Code
test: Open each API service's workflow definition in GitHub Actions and confirm a non-skippable spec-generation step runs per build
Download the OpenAPI artifact from the latest successful run in GitHub Actions and note its version and commit SHA
Call five sampled live endpoints via the API gateway and compare field names, types and status codes against the spec artifact
Push a branch removing a required field annotation in GitHub Enterprise and open the resulting checks on the pull request
Pass when the generation step is mandatory, the 5 endpoints show zero discrepancies, and the spec-diff check blocks the merge

standards.name: Auto-Scaling Configured
test: Open each production service's Auto Scaling group in the AWS console and record thresholds, min/max counts and cooldown periods
Open three months of CPU, request-rate and queue-depth metrics in CloudWatch covering enrollment, renewal and surge windows
Open the latest peak load test report in Confluence and confirm the service scaled automatically within the documented time
Export incident records from ServiceNow ITSM for the test window and check for manual scaling intervention tickets
Open the 12-month scaling policy change history in GitHub Enterprise and confirm each threshold change cites observed load data
Pass when no policy uses platform defaults, thresholds match observed peaks, scaling was automatic and changes carry rationale

standards.name: Automated Deployment to Dev on Merge
test: Open the integration branch workflow in GitHub Actions and confirm merge events trigger a dev deploy with no manual approval gate
Open the 30-day deployment history in GitHub Actions and select five merged pull requests
Open each selected run log in GitHub Actions and confirm the dev deploy started on merge and completed without manual steps
Open the dev environment version endpoint and compare the running artifact version to the integration branch HEAD commit
Record on the team page in Confluence written confirmations from the QA team and one integration partner team of reliance on it
Pass when all five merges auto-deployed successfully, dev matches HEAD, and both written confirmations are on record

standards.name: Automated Discovery Preferred
test: Open the lineage settings in Microsoft Purview and confirm automated collection is enabled for all active production pipelines
Run the lineage coverage report in Microsoft Purview and check automated events cover at least 90% of pipeline runs in 30 days
Filter manual lineage entries in Microsoft Purview and check each lists a named owner and a review date within 90 days
Open five end-to-end lineage graphs for critical datasets in Microsoft Purview and trace each from source to consumer for gaps
Pass when coverage is at least 90%, zero manual entries lack an owner or a 90-day review, and all 5 graphs are complete

standards.name: Automated Regression Detection
test: Open the pipeline definition in GitHub Actions and locate the regression step, its stored baseline and statistical threshold
Open the last 10 pipeline runs in GitHub Actions and confirm each compared performance results against the recorded baseline
Find one flagged regression among the 10 runs in GitHub Actions and confirm the build was blocked from promotion
Open the linked change record in ServiceNow ITSM and confirm a resolution or a named-approver acceptance with justification
Check the baseline artifact date in GitHub Actions and confirm it was updated within the current release cycle
Pass when the check exists, all 10 runs compared to baseline, and every flag was blocked then resolved or formally accepted

standards.name: Automated Tests for Architecture Compliance
test: Open the pipeline configs for three delivery teams in GitHub Actions and locate fitness function stages run on every build or PR
Open the rule set files in GitHub Enterprise and confirm rules for dependency direction, banned libraries, isolation and latency
Open a recent run for each team in GitHub Actions and confirm per-rule pass/fail results report beside unit and integration tests
Push a branch importing a prohibited library in GitHub Enterprise and confirm the check fails, names the rule and blocks merge
Open the reference architecture page in Confluence and compare each documented constraint against the encoded rule set for gaps
Pass when all 3 teams run the rules on every build, the seeded violation fails and blocks merge, and no constraint is unencoded

standards.name: Azure Service Bus and Kafka for Event Streaming
test: Open the integration catalogue in Confluence and check every entry names Service Bus or Kafka with a linked selection record
Filter the catalogue in Confluence for unsanctioned brokers such as RabbitMQ or out-of-policy SQS and flag any hits
Open three Service Bus namespaces in the Azure portal and verify private endpoints plus SAS or managed-identity authentication
Open the config for three Kafka clusters in Confluent Control Center and confirm TLS in transit with SASL/SCRAM or mutual TLS
Open the pattern guidance in GitHub Enterprise and confirm a 12-month review and correct Kafka vs Service Bus use-case mapping
Pass when all integrations use sanctioned brokers with selection records and sampled configs meet auth and encryption settings

standards.name: Blue-Green or Canary Deployments
test: Export the 90-day production deployment history from GitHub Actions and classify each release as blue-green, canary or in-place
Open the promotion gates for three canary releases in GitHub Actions and record the error-rate and latency thresholds configured
Pull traffic-routing logs for the sampled releases from the service mesh and verify the 5-10% initial split before promotion
Open the load-balancer routing rules in the service mesh console and confirm quoting, billing and claims endpoints are covered
Open the rollback job for each sampled release in GitHub Actions and confirm it exists and was tested
Pass when zero in-place replacements occurred and all 3 canaries gated on thresholds before 100% promotion with rollback ready

standards.name: Breaking Changes Require Consumer Notification
test: Open the change log in the API catalog and select the three most recent releases tagged as breaking changes
Open the consumer registry notifications in the API catalog and confirm dated records cover 100% of consumers before each release
Open each release ticket in Jira and confirm a migration window with start and end dates that had not closed before promotion
Open the release-approval record in Jira and confirm acknowledgment artifacts from all affected external distribution partners
Search the API catalog for any breaking deployment in the last 12 months lacking a consumer-notification record
Pass when all 3 releases show full notification, valid migration windows and partner acknowledgments, with zero undocumented cases

standards.name: Builds Under 15 Minutes
test: Export 30 days of build durations for all pipelines from GitHub Actions and compute median and 95th percentile per pipeline
List pipelines whose 95th percentile exceeds 15 minutes and open the matching remediation items in Jira for owner and target date
Open the stage-breakdown logs of five over-limit runs in GitHub Actions and confirm the breaching stage is named in the Jira item
Open the workflow files of two representative services in GitHub Enterprise and confirm cache directives and parallel stages
Pass when every pipeline's median and 95th percentile are under 15 minutes or an owned, dated remediation item exists

standards.name: Business Case Required
test: Select five active initiatives in the PPM tool (Clarity) and open the approved business case attached to each
Check each case in the PPM tool (Clarity) for populated problem statement, benefits, cost estimate and strategic alignment
Open the PMO tiering guidance in Confluence and confirm each case's depth matches its investment tier, such as NPV for Tier 1
Compare the approval signature date on each case in the PPM tool (Clarity) against the initiative's portfolio entry date
Pass when 100% of the 5 cases are complete, tier-appropriate and approved by the designated authority before portfolio entry

standards.name: Business Glossary Linked
test: Randomly select ten technical assets from governed domains in the enterprise data catalog (Collibra) and open each entry
Follow each asset's glossary link in the data catalog (Collibra) and confirm an approved definition with a named business steward
Open the glossary governance log in the data catalog (Collibra) and find one 12-month term change with request, approval and date
Open five carrier terms such as written premium and incurred loss in the catalog and confirm business-side steward assignments
Pass when all ten assets link to approved stewarded terms, the change followed governance, and no steward is an IT title

standards.name: Business Glossary Terms Linked
test: Sample 20 catalog entries across P&C, Life & Retirement and group benefits domains in the enterprise data catalog (Collibra)
Open each sampled entry's glossary link in the data catalog (Collibra) and confirm it resolves to an approved term, none broken
Open each linked term in the data catalog (Collibra) and confirm one canonical definition with no unresolved cross-LOB variants
Open the 90-day stewardship log in the data catalog (Collibra) and check every disputed term for a dated resolution and steward
Pass when all 20 entries resolve to single approved definitions and every dispute in the log shows a dated resolution outcome

standards.name: C4 Diagrams Maintained
test: Open each in-scope system's documentation folder in GitHub Enterprise and locate C4 Context and Container diagram sources
Compare each Container diagram against the integration registry in Confluence for billing, document and warehouse connections
Open the diagram commit history in GitHub Enterprise and match updates to material architecture changes over the past 6 months
Confirm in GitHub Enterprise that each matched diagram update was committed within 30 days of its architecture change
Pass when every system has both diagrams, no production integration is missing, and updates followed changes within 30 days

standards.name: C4 Model (Context, Container, Component, Code)
test: Open a recent solution design in Confluence and locate a labeled C4 Context diagram showing users, insurers and adjacent systems
Review the same design in Confluence for a Container diagram naming all deployable units with technology labels and links
Check in Confluence that container-to-container communication is complete and consistent with the Context view
Where Component or Code diagrams appear in Confluence, confirm each drills into a container named in the parent view
Pass when Context and Container views are present, complete and consistent, and any deeper diagrams trace to a named container
